prompt: Which Argo CD component writes to the cluster?

choices.text: The application controller
choices.why: Right. It compares and applies, and is the only part with write access.

choices.text: The API server behind the CLI
choices.why: It answers the CLI and the web interface and asks the controller to act.

choices.text: Redis, the shared cache
choices.why: It is a cache for the other two.

choices.text: The repo server that renders manifests
choices.why: It clones and renders, and holds no cluster credentials at all.

prompt: Why does it matter that the repo server holds no credentials to the cluster?

choices.text: Gitea forbids it
choices.why: Gitea knows nothing about Argo CD's components.

choices.text: It would be slower with credentials
choices.why: Credentials do not affect rendering speed.

choices.text: It caches manifests in Redis, which is public
choices.why: Redis is inside the cluster and not public.

choices.text: It renders whatever a repository asks for, trusted or not
choices.why: Right. A malicious chart or plugin reaches the repo server first, and finds no key there.

prompt: One Argo CD ___ is one arrow from a place in Git to a place in the cluster.
Why does the lesson apply Argo CD with --server-side?

choices.text: Without it, the images are pulled from quay.io
choices.why: Image names come from the kustomization, not from the apply mode.

choices.text: Server-side apply is how a namespace is set
choices.why: Kustomize sets the namespace in this lesson.

choices.text: Client-side apply does not read URLs
choices.why: Kustomize fetches the URL either way.

choices.text: Its CRDs are too large for the annotation a client-side apply stores
choices.why: Right. A client-side apply stores the whole object in an annotation, which has a size limit.

prompt: The kustomization names install.yaml at v3.5.4. What does pinning the version buy?

choices.text: Faster downloads from GitHub
choices.why: The size is the same either way.

choices.text: The same URL always gives the same bytes
choices.why: Right. An upgrade becomes a reviewed one-line change.

choices.text: The installation skips the CRDs
choices.why: The CRDs are part of install.yaml at any version.

choices.text: Argo CD upgrades itself on each sync
choices.why: Pinning does the opposite; nothing upgrades on its own.

prompt: What does argocd login --core change about how the command works?

choices.text: It disables the application controller
choices.why: The controller keeps running; the CLI just reads its objects directly.

choices.text: It logs in as the admin user with the generated password
choices.why: That is the normal login, through the API server.

choices.text: It goes through your kubeconfig instead
choices.why: Right. No password, port-forward or ingress, at the price of needing cluster access.

choices.text: It installs the core components into the cluster
choices.why: Installing was the kubectl apply; login changes nothing in the cluster.

prompt: Which Gitea permission does the argocd account have on fleet?

choices.text: admin
choices.why: Nothing in this course gives a machine account admin.

choices.text: write
choices.why: That is Bruno's and ci's, which can push branches.

choices.text: owner
choices.why: Only Ana owns fleet.

choices.text: read
choices.why: Right. Argo CD never pushes, opens or approves anything.

prompt: argocd repo add stored the token where?

choices.text: In a Secret in the cluster
choices.why: Right. A repository is a Secret with the argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: repository label.

choices.text: In ~/.git-credentials on your machine
choices.why: That file is Git's, for your own pushes.

choices.text: In Gitea, beside the argocd account
choices.why: Gitea keeps tokens of its own; Argo CD keeps its copy in the cluster.

choices.text: In the Application's spec
choices.why: The Application names the repository URL, never its credentials.

prompt: A teammate proposes committing the repository Secret's YAML to fleet so the setup is fully in Git. What is wrong?

choices.text: The label would be stripped by Kustomize
choices.why: Kustomize keeps labels.

choices.text: Gitea refuses YAML files that contain tokens
choices.why: Gitea stores whatever is pushed.

choices.text: Argo CD skips Secrets found in Git
choices.why: It applies any manifest, Secrets included; that is the danger.

choices.text: base64 is an encoding, not encryption
choices.why: Right. Lesson 9 shows how to keep it in Git encrypted instead.

prompt: The first Application reported OutOfSync though the manifests matched what was deployed. Why?

choices.text: The image tag in Git was newer
choices.why: Git and the cluster both said 1.0.

choices.text: reconcile.sh had changed the replicas
choices.why: The diff showed no replicas line.

choices.text: The namespace had been deleted
choices.why: Health was Healthy; the objects were all there.

choices.text: A missing tracking annotation
choices.why: Right. The diff showed only argocd.argoproj.io/tracking-id.

prompt: What does the tracking annotation make possible that lesson 1's loop could not do?

choices.text: Pruning what left Git
choices.why: Right. Objects that carry the id and are no longer in Git can be found and deleted.

choices.text: Rendering Kustomize
choices.why: The repo server renders whether or not objects are tracked.

choices.text: Running without cluster credentials
choices.why: The controller still needs them to apply.

choices.text: Reading a private repository
choices.why: That needs credentials, not an annotation.

prompt: Why does the lesson tell you to stop reconcile.sh before creating the Application?

choices.text: Argo CD refuses to start while the loop runs
choices.why: Argo CD does not know the loop exists.

choices.text: Two writers would race for one object
choices.why: Right. Even reading the same repository, two writers race and confuse ownership.

choices.text: reconcile.sh would delete the Application
choices.why: It only applies the staging directory.

choices.text: The loop uses the argocd token
choices.why: It used Ana's credentials.

prompt: Match each combination of sync and health to what it usually means.

pairs.right: A change not applied yet, or drift

prompt: Staging is Synced and Degraded after a merge. Where is the fault most likely to be?

choices.text: In what the repository says
choices.why: Right. Argo CD applied it faithfully; the bug is in Git, like lesson 2's missing image.

choices.text: In Gitea's branch protection
choices.why: Protection governs merges, not running pods.

choices.text: In Argo CD's controller
choices.why: A failing controller would leave the application OutOfSync or Unknown.

choices.text: In the repo server's cache
choices.why: A stale cache shows the wrong revision, not a degraded object.

prompt: After a sync, where does the answer to 'which commit is staging running?' come from?

choices.text: The newest commit on main
choices.why: main may have moved since the last sync.

choices.text: The Application's status
choices.why: Right. It records the revision it applied.

choices.text: The image tag
choices.why: The tag names an image, not a commit of fleet.

choices.text: Gitea's list of merged pull requests
choices.why: That says what was merged, not what was applied.

prompt: Which of these does the sync policy prune: true, selfHeal: true add to automated sync? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Syncing when the cluster drifts from Git
choices.why: Right. That is selfHeal.

choices.text: Deleting objects that disappeared from Git
choices.why: Right. That is prune.

choices.text: Rolling back when a pod becomes Degraded
choices.why: Nothing rolls back on health; Argo CD applies Git.

choices.text: Looking at Git more often than every three minutes
choices.why: The interval is a separate setting, or a webhook.

prompt: By default, every how many minutes does Argo CD look at a repository for new commits?
Right after the merge, argocd app get still showed the old revision. What made it see the new one at once?

choices.text: argocd app get --refresh
choices.why: Right. It asks Argo CD to look now, and the automated policy synced in the same pass.

choices.text: argocd app sync with --prune
choices.why: Syncing applies what Argo CD already rendered; it needs a refresh first.

choices.text: Restarting the repo server
choices.why: That would work eventually, and is not what the lesson did.

choices.text: Pushing the commit a second time
choices.why: A second push of the same commit changes nothing.

prompt: With prune on, somebody deletes staging/bulletin.yaml by mistake and it is merged. What happens?

choices.text: Nothing until somebody syncs by hand
choices.why: The policy is automated.

choices.text: Only the Service is removed
choices.why: Every object in the deleted file goes.

choices.text: The objects are deleted in the cluster
choices.why: Right. A file gone from Git is an object gone from the cluster; the review is the guard.

choices.text: Argo CD refuses an empty render
choices.why: That protects against a path that vanishes, not a file deleted inside it.

prompt: Why did Argo CD revert the manual scale faster than lesson 1's loop did?

choices.text: kubectl scale is slower under Argo CD
choices.why: kubectl took effect at once; Argo CD undid it.

choices.text: Its interval is shorter than fifteen seconds
choices.why: Its Git interval is three minutes.

choices.text: It reacts to events, not to a timer
choices.why: Right. selfHeal does not wait for the Git timer.

choices.text: It polls the cluster each second
choices.why: It watches; it does not poll the cluster on a timer.

prompt: An autoscaler owns replicas for one Deployment. What is the narrowest correct response?

choices.text: Delete the autoscaler
choices.why: It is the right owner of replicas; Git is the wrong one.

choices.text: Ignore the whole Deployment object
choices.why: The image, probes and the rest would go unreconciled.

choices.text: Ignore that one field, and respect it on sync
choices.why: Right. One field, one kind: the hole is exactly as wide as the owner.

choices.text: Turn selfHeal off for the whole Application
choices.why: That gives up every other field too.

prompt: Without the sync option ___=true, a sync would still overwrite a field that ignoreDifferences only hides from the comparison.
Why did argocd app rollback refuse to run on staging?

choices.text: History keeps a single entry
choices.why: It listed several entries.

choices.text: Ana lacks permission to roll back
choices.why: With --core she has the cluster's admin credentials.

choices.text: The old revision was deleted from Gitea
choices.why: Git keeps every commit; nothing was deleted.

choices.text: Auto-sync was on and would undo it
choices.why: Right. A rollback outside Git is drift by definition.

prompt: By default, how many syncs does an Application's history keep?
After the app of apps, what is left outside Git?

choices.text: Every Application except the staging one, still on your machine
choices.why: They all live in fleet/argocd/ now.

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: Something has to exist before the agent can read Git.

choices.text: The staging manifests
choices.why: They were always in fleet.

choices.text: Argo CD's installation and root.yaml
choices.why: Right. That is the bootstrap, and the goal is to keep it to two files.

prompt: With the root Application in place, how is a new application added to the cluster?

choices.text: Editing root.yaml
choices.why: root.yaml points at the directory; it does not list applications.

choices.text: A pull request adding its file to fleet/argocd/
choices.why: Right. The root applies whatever is in that directory.

choices.text: kubectl apply of the Application on your machine
choices.why: That is what the root replaced.

choices.text: argocd app create on the command line
choices.why: It works, and leaves the application outside Git.

prompt: Match each AppProject list to what it allows.
An Application in project bulletin points at kube-system. When is it stopped?

choices.text: It is not stopped; kube-system is allowed by default
choices.why: Only listed destinations are allowed in this project.

choices.text: Before any sync, when the controller validates it
choices.why: Right. The Application itself is refused, with the project named.

choices.text: During the sync, object by object
choices.why: It never gets as far as a sync.

choices.text: Only after a person rejects it in the web interface
choices.why: The rule is enforced by the controller, not by a person.

prompt: An Application's repository cannot be read. Why is its sync status Unknown rather than OutOfSync?

choices.text: Unknown means the Application was deleted
choices.why: A deleted Application has no status at all.

choices.text: The cluster is unreachable
choices.why: The cluster was fine; the repository was the problem.

choices.text: Argo CD hides failures behind Unknown
choices.why: The ComparisonError condition says exactly what happened.

choices.text: Nothing was rendered, so there is nothing to compare
choices.why: Right. OutOfSync is a comparison result, and there was no comparison.

prompt: Why does Argo CD not prune everything when an Application's path stops existing?

choices.text: An empty render is treated as an error
choices.why: Right. A vanished path is reported as an error, and the objects stay.

choices.text: Pruning needs a person to confirm each object
choices.why: Pruning is automatic when the policy says so.

choices.text: Objects outside the path keep their tracking ids
choices.why: They keep them either way; the safeguard is about the render.

choices.text: Git refuses to delete a directory
choices.why: Directories can be deleted like any file.

prompt: Order what happened when the staging message changed in this lesson.
items: argocd app get still shows the old revision
argocd app get --refresh finds the new commit
trap: Argo CD does not know about the merge until it looks, and it syncs only what it has seen.

prompt: A chart you do not control sets replicas, an autoscaler also sets it, and selfHeal keeps fighting. What should change, and where?

choices.text: The cluster: scale it by hand after each sync
choices.why: Every sync, or self-heal, would undo it.

choices.text: The Application, in Git: ignore that one field
choices.why: Right. The chart cannot change, so the Application narrows what it compares, through a pull request.

choices.text: The autoscaler: delete it so Git wins
choices.why: Then load decides nothing, which defeats having one.

choices.text: Argo CD: turn off selfHeal globally
choices.why: That gives up drift correction for every application.

prompt: What does Redis do in an Argo CD installation?

choices.text: Holds the repository credentials
choices.why: Those are Secrets in the argocd namespace.

choices.text: Stores the Applications
choices.why: Applications are Kubernetes objects.

choices.text: Runs the sync operations
choices.why: The application controller does that.

choices.text: Caches renders and live state between comparisons
choices.why: Right. So a comparison does not clone and render everything again.

prompt: kubectl apply without --server-side refuses Argo CD's manifests. Why?

choices.text: Client-side apply cannot create namespaces
choices.why: It can.

choices.text: The cluster blocks client-side apply
choices.why: Nothing blocks it in general.

choices.text: Its CRDs exceed the annotation a client-side apply stores
choices.why: Right. Server-side apply keeps no such annotation.

choices.text: The manifests are not valid YAML
choices.why: They are valid; only too large for that annotation.

prompt: Argo CD's Gitea token leaks. What can somebody do with it?

choices.text: Change the cluster
choices.why: The token reaches Gitea, not the cluster.

choices.text: Read fleet
choices.why: Right. It has read:repository and nothing more.

choices.text: Push to main
choices.why: The token cannot write, and main is protected anyway.

choices.text: Approve pull requests
choices.why: Approving needs write permission.

prompt: In an Application, what does destination.server https://kubernetes.default.svc mean?

choices.text: A cluster on the public internet
choices.why: It is the in-cluster address of the API server.

choices.text: The Gitea server
choices.why: Gitea is the source, not the destination.

choices.text: The registry
choices.why: Registries are never a destination.

choices.text: The cluster Argo CD itself runs in
choices.why: Right. Other clusters are registered by address.

prompt: Match each combination to what it usually means.

pairs.right: Git describes what runs, and it works
Git changed and nothing applied it yet
Git was applied, and what it says does not work

prompt: What shortens the three-minute wait between a merge and Argo CD noticing it?

choices.text: A shorter revisionHistoryLimit
choices.why: That limits history, not polling.

choices.text: A webhook from the Git server on every push
choices.why: Right. The wait drops to a second or two.

choices.text: Turning selfHeal on
choices.why: selfHeal reacts to the cluster, not to Git.

choices.text: More replicas of the repo server
choices.why: Polling interval is not about capacity.

prompt: Why does Argo CD undo a manual scale faster than lesson 1's loop?

choices.text: It polls every second
choices.why: It does not poll the cluster on a short timer.

choices.text: It watches the objects and reacts to the change as an event
choices.why: Right. The loop only noticed on its next timed pass.

choices.text: It locks the Deployment
choices.why: Nothing is locked.

choices.text: kubectl asks Argo CD before scaling
choices.why: kubectl talks only to the API server.

prompt: With automated sync off, argocd app rollback works. What state does it leave?

choices.text: Synced, and the old revision becomes main
choices.why: main is unchanged.

choices.text: Degraded, until a resync
choices.why: Health depends on the objects, not on the rollback.

choices.text: Synced, with Git rewritten
choices.why: Argo CD never writes to Git.

choices.text: OutOfSync until Git is fixed
choices.why: Right. Honest, and the fix still belongs in Git.

prompt: After the app of apps, what is still outside Git?

choices.text: The staging manifests
choices.why: They were always in Git.

choices.text: Every Application
choices.why: They are all in argocd/ now.

choices.text: root.yaml and the Argo CD installation
choices.why: Right. The bootstrap, kept to two files.

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: Something has to exist before the agent can read Git.

prompt: The bulletin project allows only Namespace among cluster-scoped kinds. What would be refused?

choices.text: A Service in production
choices.why: Namespaced, in an allowed destination.

choices.text: A ClusterRole
choices.why: Right. Cluster-scoped and not on the list.

choices.text: The staging Namespace
choices.why: Namespace is on the list.

choices.text: A Deployment in staging
choices.why: Namespaced, in an allowed destination.
